intent: Change one sensing factor set at a time: widen the array from ±0.02 to ±0.03 m so tape stays under a sensor out to about 0.036 m of drift, and bring the row from 4 cm to 2 cm ahead of the axle to cut lookahead lag and oscillation. Expect fewer line-loss events, a max_error below the 0.06 m off-track limit on the slalom and s-bend, and higher progress than the baseline's 0.10 to 0.19.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the baseline's off-track ends came from the array losing the tape at about 0.02 m of drift, so a ±0.03 m spread should cut line-loss events to near zero; (2) moving the row to y = 0.02 lowers steering_oscillation at similar rms_error, which would confirm the lookahead lag; (3) if max_error still reaches 0.06 on the slalom with no line loss, the limiting factor is controller gain or base speed, not geometry. Ask the Integrator whether the signal saturates at the outer sensors with the 15 mm spacing, whether kd can drop now that the lookahead is shorter, and whether the robot still stalls before completing the course.
rationale: The baseline ended every run off track at max_error about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit (the body-width term is only 0.0425 m at width 0.12, so the floor of 0.06 applies). Progress was only 0.10 to 0.19, so the robot is leaving the tape early on every track. Line-loss events of 1 to 2 per run and oscillation of 0.07 to 0.16 point at the sensor array, not only at the controller. The 10 mm spacing with 12 mm footprints spans only about ±0.02 m, so when the robot drifts about 3 cm the tape leaves the array. The 4 cm forward offset also gives a long lookahead, which adds lag on the bends. I widen the outer sensors to ±0.03 m, which keeps tape under a sensor out to about 0.036 m of drift, and keep five sensors at 15 mm spacing so the centre still resolves small offsets. I move the row from y = 0.04 to y = 0.02 to shorten the lookahead and reduce the overshoot that drove the oscillation. Body width stays at 0.12 because any width from 0.08 to 0.18 leaves the off-track limit at 0.06 m, so it gives no benefit. The wheel track and radius stay as in the baseline so the change is isolated to sensing. I expect fewer line-loss events, a lower max_error, and more progress, while completion time depends on the controller's base speed.
